items.prompt:
Text: 'The heart pumps blood through the body. It beats about 100 times a minute when you exercise.'
Image: A diagram shows a heart with two arrows: one going in and one going out. The label says 'blood in' and 'blood out.'

What is the main idea that BOTH the text and the image are trying to explain? Use details from both to support your answer.
items.answer: The main idea is that the heart's job is to move blood through the body. The text explains this and adds that it beats faster during exercise. The image shows the direction blood flows in and out, which supports the idea that the heart keeps blood moving.

steps: Find the main idea shared by both: the heart moves blood.
The text says the heart pumps blood and beats faster when you exercise.
The image shows arrows for blood going in and out of the heart.
Both are explaining the same job: the heart keeps blood moving through the body.
Together they show the main idea from two different angles.

items.prompt:
Text: 'Penguins are birds, but they cannot fly. They live in cold places and are very good swimmers.'
Image: A photo shows a group of penguins standing on ice. Some penguins are jumping into the blue water below.

A student says: 'The image does not really help because we already know penguins cannot fly.' Do you agree or disagree? Explain your thinking.
items.answer: I disagree. The image does add new information. It shows penguins jumping into the water, which supports the text's idea that they are good swimmers. It also shows the icy environment, which supports the idea that penguins live in cold places. The image adds visual proof for two details from the text.

steps: The student says the image does not help because we know penguins cannot fly.
But the image is not about flying. Look at what the image actually shows.
The image shows penguins on ice (cold place) and jumping into water (swimming).
The text says penguins live in cold places and are good swimmers.
The image adds visual support for those two ideas, so it does help.

items.prompt:
Text: 'A food chain shows what animals eat. Grass is eaten by a rabbit. The rabbit is eaten by a fox.'
Image: A diagram shows three images in a row connected by arrows: grass, then a rabbit, then a fox. Each arrow points to the right.

What does the direction of the arrows in the image tell you? Could you understand the same thing from the text alone?
items.answer: The arrows show the direction of energy, meaning who eats whom. The arrows go from grass to rabbit to fox, showing that each thing is eaten by the next. The text says the same thing in words, but the arrows in the image make the order and direction much clearer and faster to understand.

steps: Look at the arrows: they point from grass to rabbit to fox.
Arrows pointing right show the order: grass is eaten first, then rabbit, then fox.
The text describes the same chain in words.
The arrows make the direction and order clear at a glance.
The text alone would work, but the image makes understanding faster and clearer.

items.prompt:
Text: 'Nurses work in hospitals and clinics. They take care of patients by checking temperatures, giving medicine, and helping doctors.'
Image: A drawing shows a nurse in scrubs taking a patient's temperature with a thermometer. A tray with medicine cups is on the table beside them.

If the image was removed from this text, what key idea would be hardest to understand? Why?
items.answer: Without the image, it would be hardest to understand what 'taking care of patients' actually looks like in practice. The text lists the tasks, but the image shows a specific moment: the nurse using a thermometer and having medicine ready. That visual makes the job concrete and easier to picture.

steps: Think about what the text explains and what it leaves vague.
The text says nurses check temperatures and give medicine, but does not describe how.
The image shows the nurse holding a thermometer and a tray of medicine.
Without the image, 'checking temperatures' and 'giving medicine' are abstract ideas.
The image makes those tasks visible and concrete.

items.prompt:
Text: 'The water cycle has three main steps. Water evaporates from oceans and lakes. It forms clouds in the sky. Then it falls back down as rain or snow.'
Image: A diagram shows a large body of water on the left. Upward arrows show water rising as steam. A cloud is in the middle at the top. Downward arrows show rain falling on the right, into a river that flows back to the large body of water.

What does the image show about the water cycle that the text does not fully explain?
items.answer: The image shows that the water cycle goes in a loop: the rain flows back into the ocean and starts again. The text lists three steps but does not say the cycle repeats. The image shows the river connecting back to the ocean, which means the process never really stops.

steps: The text lists three steps: evaporation, clouds, rain/snow.
The image shows all three steps but also shows a river flowing from the rain back to the ocean.
The river going back to the ocean shows the cycle repeats.
The text says three steps but does not say it repeats.
The image adds the key idea that the cycle is continuous.

items.prompt:
Text: 'Animals that hibernate sleep through the winter. Bears eat a lot in autumn to store fat, then sleep until spring.'
Image: A drawing shows a bear curled up inside a cave with snow outside the cave entrance. The trees outside have no leaves.

How do details in the image work together to support the main idea of the text?
items.answer: The image shows a bear curled up (sleeping), inside a cave (sheltered), with snow outside (winter) and bare trees (no food available). All these details together support the main idea that bears sleep through winter in a safe place when food is scarce.

steps: The main idea is that animals hibernate through winter.
The bear is curled up: it is sleeping (hibernating).
The cave provides shelter for the long sleep.
The snow and bare trees show it is winter.
All four details together build a complete picture of hibernation.

items.prompt:
Text: 'The sun is a star. It looks bigger than other stars because it is much closer to Earth.'
Image: A diagram shows a large yellow circle labeled 'Sun' on the left and tiny dots labeled 'Other stars' far to the right. A line shows the distance from Earth (a small blue dot in the middle) to each.

What is the key idea that the diagram helps explain? Why would words alone be difficult to explain this idea?
items.answer: The key idea is that the sun looks big because it is close, not because it actually is bigger than all stars. Words alone are difficult because it is hard to explain relative distances without showing them. The diagram makes the distance obvious by showing how far the other stars are compared to the sun.

steps: The text says the sun looks bigger because it is closer to Earth.
The diagram shows a large sun close to Earth and tiny dots (stars) far away.
The distance lines in the diagram show the difference in how far away each is.
Words like 'much closer' are hard to visualize without a picture.
The diagram makes the distance comparison concrete and easy to see.

items.prompt:
Text: 'Firefighters wear special gear to stay safe. They wear helmets, thick coats, heavy boots, and air tanks on their backs.'
Image: A labeled diagram of a firefighter shows arrows pointing to: a yellow helmet, a thick gray coat, heavy black boots, and a silver air tank on the back.

A student says: 'The image just shows the same things the words say.' Is this a fair criticism? What does the image add beyond repeating the words?
items.answer: It is partly fair because the image shows the same gear mentioned in the text. But the image adds more: it shows where each piece of gear goes on the body, what each piece looks like, and how they all work together as a full outfit. The text names the parts but the image shows the complete picture of a firefighter ready for work.

steps: The student says both text and image say the same thing.
Check: both name the same four pieces of gear. That is true.
But does the image add anything? Look more carefully.
The image shows where each piece goes on the body.
It also shows what each piece looks like (shape, color).
And it shows them all together as a complete firefighter uniform.
The text names parts; the image shows a whole, working picture.

items.prompt:
Text: 'Flowers attract bees with bright colors and sweet smells. The bee drinks nectar from the flower and picks up yellow powder called pollen.'
Image: A drawing shows a bee inside a large flower. The bee has yellow dots (pollen) on its fuzzy legs. Curved arrows show the bee moving from one flower to another.

The image shows the bee moving from flower to flower, but the text does not mention this. Why might the author have chosen to include this in the image?
items.answer: The author probably included the bee moving from flower to flower to show that the bee spreads pollen to other flowers. This is the important result of the bee's visit, which connects to why flowers attract bees. The image hints at a bigger idea: bees help plants grow by moving pollen around.

steps: The text says the bee drinks nectar and picks up pollen.
The image adds arrows showing the bee flying to another flower.
Why show the bee moving? Because when the bee goes to a new flower, it brings pollen.
Bringing pollen to a new flower helps that flower make seeds.
The author added this to hint at the bigger purpose: bees help flowers.

items.prompt:
Text: 'Rain forests are home to more kinds of animals and plants than any other place on Earth. They get a lot of rain all year long.'
Image: A drawing shows tall trees with thick green leaves covering the top (labeled 'canopy'). Below are smaller trees and plants. Animals are shown at different levels: birds at the top, monkeys in the middle, and a jaguar on the ground.

What key idea does the image add about life in the rain forest that the text does not explain?
items.answer: The image adds the key idea that different animals live at different levels of the rain forest. The text says many animals live there, but the image shows that birds live in the canopy, monkeys live in the middle, and jaguars live on the ground. Each animal has its own layer.

steps: The text says rain forests have many kinds of animals.
The image shows animals at three different levels: canopy, middle, ground.
The text does not mention that animals use different layers.
The image adds the key idea that the rain forest is organized into layers, each with different animals.
This is important information that makes the rain forest easier to understand.

items.prompt:
Text: 'A compass helps people know which direction they are going. It always points north.'
Image: A drawing shows a circular compass with the letters N, S, E, W at four points. A red arrow needle points toward the N.

If a student only looked at the image and did not read the text, what could they figure out on their own? What would they still need the text to explain?
items.answer: From the image alone, a student could figure out that the compass has four directions labeled N, S, E, W and that the red needle points to N. They would still need the text to explain that it always points north and that it is used to help people find their direction when traveling.

steps: Look at the image by itself: what information does it give?
The image shows the four direction letters and a red arrow pointing to N.
A student can see the arrow points north.
But the text tells you WHY it points north and what a compass is FOR.
The text adds the purpose and the always-north rule that the image cannot show.

items.prompt:
Text: 'Soil is made of tiny bits of rock, dead plants, and living creatures like worms. Plants grow in soil because it has nutrients they need.'
Image: A cross-section diagram shows layers of soil. The top layer is dark brown with roots growing through it and a worm visible. The middle layer is lighter brown with small rocks. The bottom layer is solid rock.

What does the cross-section format of the image let you understand that a regular photo could not show?
items.answer: A cross-section cuts the soil open to show what is inside layer by layer. A regular photo of the ground surface would only show what is on top. The cross-section lets you see the dark top layer with roots and worms, the middle layer with rocks, and the solid rock underneath, all of which the text describes.

steps: A regular photo shows the surface of the ground but not what is underneath.
A cross-section cuts the soil open to show the inside layers.
The image shows three layers: dark top, lighter middle, solid rock bottom.
This helps us see that soil has layers, which a surface photo could not show.
The cross-section matches the text's description of what soil is made of.

items.prompt:
Text: 'Astronauts work on the International Space Station. They float because there is very little gravity in space.'
Image: A photo shows an astronaut floating sideways inside the space station. Tools and bags float in the air around the astronaut.

How does the image prove the text's claim that astronauts float in space?
items.answer: The image proves the claim by showing an actual astronaut floating sideways with objects floating around them. In normal gravity, the astronaut and objects would be standing or sitting on the floor. The image shows the evidence that floating really happens in the space station.

steps: The text claims astronauts float because there is little gravity.
The image shows an astronaut sideways in the air with objects floating too.
On Earth, people stand on the floor and objects fall down.
In the image, neither the astronaut nor the objects are on the floor.
The image provides visual proof of the floating described in the text.

items.prompt:
Text: 'Honeycombs are made of six-sided shapes called hexagons. Bees build honeycombs to store honey and raise their young.'
Image: A close-up photo shows a honeycomb filled with six-sided cells. Some cells are sealed with wax. Others are open and appear to be filled with golden honey.

What mathematical detail does the image show that helps you understand why bees might use hexagons?
items.answer: The image shows that hexagons fit together perfectly with no gaps or wasted space. All the cells are the same size and fit side by side. This suggests bees use hexagons because they are the most efficient shape to fill space without any waste, which helps them store as much honey as possible.

steps: The text says honeycombs are made of hexagon shapes.
The image shows many hexagons fitted together with no space between them.
No gaps means no wasted space in the honeycomb.
Bees can store more honey when there is no wasted space.
The image suggests bees use hexagons because they are efficient space-fillers.

items.prompt:
Text: 'Community gardens are places where neighbors share a piece of land to grow vegetables and flowers together.'
Image: A photo shows a large garden divided into small squares by low wooden fences. Different plants grow in each square. Several people of different ages are working in different squares.

What key ideas from the text does EACH visual detail in the image support? Match each visual detail to a key idea.
items.answer: The large shared land supports 'a piece of land.' The squares separated by fences support 'neighbors share' because each person or family has their own section. Different plants in each square support 'grow vegetables and flowers.' People of different ages working together supports 'neighbors' working together in a community.

steps: Key idea 1: shared piece of land. Visual: the large garden space in the photo.
Key idea 2: neighbors share. Visual: the squares divided by fences show different people's sections.
Key idea 3: grow vegetables and flowers. Visual: different plants growing in different squares.
Key idea 4: neighbors (community). Visual: people of different ages working together.
Each visual detail connects to a specific word or idea in the text.
